methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pipedream is a Series A transportation company that has raised $22.4M to date. The broader transportation sector includes eight private peer companies—notably Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, FleetZero, and Parallel Systems—though no public comparables exist. The peer set is too dispersed in stage and valuation tier to support a reliable median-based approach; same-stage and adjacent-stage peers number below the three-company threshold needed for robust peer analysis.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation lens. Using total raised ($22.4M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $44.8M. This reflects the capital base and expected value creation between current and next financing rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $38M (low) to $52M (high), with a median of $45M. This single-method triangulation carries material uncertainty: the range reflects parametric sensitivity around the step-up multiplier rather than cross-validation against peer trading multiples or comparable transaction data. Key unknowns include unit economics, path to profitability, and market traction relative to the broader transportation peer set. A more robust valuation would require either identification of narrower stage-matched comparables or disclosure of Pipedream's revenue, growth, or burn metrics.
